title: Visiting musicians, teaching kids, and the school-board jazz curriculum project
summary: Cannonball Adderley and local players came to hear the group, kids were brought in to sit in, and the school board backed a project pairing the quartet with Alvin Alcorn and poetry as a seed for NOCA.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: if you're involved in the evolution of a music, then naturally you would have to go back and study the music from its inception or from its very beginning and find out what all the masters that came before, so that you would have a chronological insight, a chronological appreciation from a student's standpoint to know the lineage of the drummers, the lineage of the soprano, saxophone players, clarinetists, and so on through all the instruments, and to see how what we were playing at that time, which was often thought of as being rather avant-garde, and we were playing sometimes tonally, but at the other aspect we were playing changes and we were playing conventional chord changes and conventional tunes. We'd take, I remember April, and we were always playing the right changes at the right time, but we would take it some other places, and David Lee was playing other kind of stuff, metrically, because you would hear David play and think that you were hearing two or three drummers because he could play and imply one thing and have something else going on with the bass drum, but it was so contrapuntal or multi-metric, but the basic pulse would always be there.
